key_insight: Routine clinical data available by the first echocardiogram can help shortlist likely genetic diagnoses in infants with congenital heart disease.
clinical_relevance: This could support earlier genetic referral or testing prioritization when diagnosis is unclear, but it is a decision-support tool rather than a standalone diagnostic test.
method: Retrospective single-center cohort of 1,720 children with CHD and confirmed genetic diagnoses or negative genetic workup.
Compared class-balanced logistic regression with a multimodal deep learning fusion model using echocardiogram images plus serial clinical data as they became available.
Evaluated balanced top-3 accuracy across staged inputs, with bootstrap intervals.
evidence_signal: Balanced top-3 accuracy improved from 0.758 using echocardiogram-visit inputs alone to 0.809 after adding serial records, radiology notes, and ICD-10 codes; multimodal fusion performed similarly.
watch_item: Single-center retrospective data and modest gains over logistic regression mean external validation and careful integration into clinical workflows are needed before use.
paper_title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Modeling to Aid in the Identification of Genetic Conditions in Infants with Congenital Heart Disease
